concept.name: Momentum factor
concept.definition: A stock factor that is long stocks with high recent returns and short stocks with low recent returns, formalizing the cross-sectional momentum pattern documented by Jegadeesh and Titman (1993) and incorporated into the Carhart four-factor model; in the French library, Mom is built from portfolios sorted on prior 2-12 month returns.
concept.intuition: Stocks that went up over roughly the past year (skipping the most recent month) have tended to keep outperforming recent losers for a while - the factor trades that continuation.
concept.mechanics: Ken French's Mom uses six value-weight portfolios formed monthly on size and prior (2-12) returns: Mom = (1/2)(Small High + Big High) - (1/2)(Small Low + Big Low), with NYSE median size breakpoint and 30th/70th prior-return percentiles; the most recent month is skipped to avoid short-term reversal.
concept.formula: Mom = (1/2)(Small High + Big High) - (1/2)(Small Low + Big Low), where High/Low refer to prior (t-12 to t-2) cumulative returns.
concept.failure_modes: Momentum is prone to infrequent but severe crashes when trends reverse sharply, typically in rebounds from bear markets (e.g., 2009), when the short side of crowded losers rallies violently; the standard Fama-French models exclude momentum precisely because it behaves differently.
concept.misconceptions: Momentum is not simply 'buy what went up last week': the academic factor uses 12-month formation returns skipping the most recent month, and it is a relative cross-sectional bet, not a market-direction bet.
concept.example: Ranking stocks each month on months t-12 to t-2 returns and going long the top third while shorting the bottom third yields the Mom factor; if winners return 1.5% and losers -0.5% in the next month, Mom realizes +2.0%.

citations.source: Kenneth R. French Data Library, Detail for Monthly Momentum Factor (Mom)
